# Spending per pupil

## Cambridge and Salem — the group's two smallest districts — have held the top two spots every year

In 2024–25 Cambridge spent about **$31,000 per K-12 pupil** in current
operating funds, against a five-district average near $30,000. Cambridge and
Salem, the group's two smallest districts, have traded first and second place
in all ten years shown — small districts spread fixed costs (a principal, a
building, a bus route) over fewer students, so their higher spending per pupil
is arithmetic, not inefficiency. Dollars are nominal — not adjusted for
inflation — and exclude capital projects, debt service, and interfund
transfers; see [Methods](../appendix/methods.qmd) for the definition.

```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())

import polars as pl
from plotnine import (
    aes,
    geom_line,
    geom_point,
    ggplot,
    labs,
    scale_color_manual,
    scale_x_continuous,
    scale_y_continuous,
)
from great_tables import GT, loc, md, style

import comparisons as cc

# Format axis/break values as whole dollars.
def _dollars(breaks):
    return [f"${v:,.0f}" if v is not None else "" for v in breaks]
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-spending-per-pupil
#| fig-cap: "Current operating spending per K–12 pupil (nominal dollars) by school year ending, 2016 (2015–16) through 2025 (2024–25). Source: NYS Comptroller local-government financial data; K-12 enrollment from NYSED."
g = (
    cc.spending_for(cc.GRAPH_GROUP)
    .filter(pl.col("year_end") >= 2016)
    .select("district", "year_end", "current_pp")
    .drop_nulls()
)
cambridge = g.filter(pl.col("district") == cc.FOCUS)

(
    ggplot(g, aes("year_end", "current_pp", color="district"))
    + geom_line(size=1)
    + geom_point(size=1.8)
    + geom_line(cambridge, size=2.4)  # emphasize the focus district
    + scale_color_manual(
        values=cc.PALETTE, name="", limits=cc.district_order(cc.GRAPH_GROUP)
    )
    + scale_x_continuous(breaks=list(range(2016, 2026)))
    + scale_y_continuous(labels=_dollars)
    + labs(
        x="School year ending",
        y="Current operating spending per pupil",
        title="Current operating spending per K-12 pupil, 2015–16 to 2024–25",
    )
    + cc.theme_ccs()
)
```

Every district's line rises over the decade — part of that is inflation — but
the rank order barely changes.

Where each district started, where it ended, and the decade's change:

```{python}
#| label: tbl-spending-per-pupil-change
#| tbl-cap: "Current operating spending per K–12 pupil in 2015–16 and 2024–25, with change, by district (nominal dollars)."
t = cc.spending_for(cc.GRAPH_GROUP).filter(pl.col("year_end").is_between(2016, 2025))

wide = (
    t.with_columns(
        pl.when(pl.col("region") == "Washington County").then(0).otherwise(1).alias("_rank")
    )
    .pivot(values="current_pp", index=["_rank", "region", "district"], on="year_end")
    .sort(["_rank", "district"])
    .drop("_rank")
)

wide = wide.with_columns((pl.col("2025") - pl.col("2016")).alias("chg"))

(
    GT(wide, rowname_col="district", groupname_col="region")
    .tab_header(
        title="Current operating spending per pupil",
        subtitle="School-year-ending 2016 (2015–16) and 2025 (2024–25), nominal dollars"
    )
    .fmt_currency(columns=["2016", "2025", "chg"], decimals=0)
    .tab_spanner(label="School year ending", columns=["2016", "2025"])
    .cols_label(chg=md("Change<br>2016→2025"))
    .tab_style(
        style=[style.fill(color="#FCEFB4"), style.text(weight="bold")],
        locations=[
            loc.body(rows=pl.col("district") == cc.FOCUS),
            loc.stub(rows=pl.col("district") == cc.FOCUS),
        ],
    )
    .tab_source_note(
        md(
            "**Source:** New York State Comptroller local-government financial "
            "data (expenditures); K-12 enrollment from NYSED. Current operating "
            "spending = General, Special Aid and School Lunch funds, excluding "
            "capital outlay, debt service and interfund transfers. Nominal "
            "dollars; year = school-year-ending (2025 = 2024–25)."
        )
    )
)
```

**Cambridge's spending per pupil rose about $10,000** — a middle-of-the-pack
increase (Greenwich's was largest at $12,000). What sets Cambridge apart is
where it started — near the top in 2015–16 — and where it remains in 2024–25.
Whether that level is sustainable as enrollment falls is taken up in the
[Taxes](taxes.qmd) chapter.

*For additional spending measures, see the exploratory [Spending](../exploratory/spending.qmd) chapter.*
